enumeration.method: Search all 26 main-document pages and independently enumerate small-caps Theorem labels from PDF text spans. Visually inspect all statements on pages 6, 9, 10, 16 and 23, and the supplement pointer and reference endpoint on pages 25-26. No theorem crosses a page boundary.

checks: The eleven original theorem statements remain identical to the independently validated and source-reviewed inventory; its handoff hash is unchanged.
PDF title, authors, arXiv stamp, SHA-256 and page count match the source provenance. Small-caps heading enumeration agrees with all eleven printed labels and their pages.
All 37 interface passages and four unranked source conventions were checked against the main-text PDF. Both full regression algorithms are preserved, including boundary and fallback branches.

The finalizer derives 45 direct uses and 100 related-theorem connections. A separate validator process accepts the inventory, graph, original statements, names, highlights, explanations and aggregate metrics.

White-noise and regression observation models have disjoint theorem reach except for the shared function-class prerequisite. White-noise procedures reach only Theorems 3.1-3.4; regression procedures reach only Theorems 4.1-4.4.

Theorem 2.3 uses arbitrary estimators and has no edge to the later adaptive procedures. The local-modulus interface reaches only Theorem 2.1; proof connections are not promoted to dependencies of Theorem 2.2.
Gaussian-maximum quantiles and tail calibration constants have no observation-model prerequisite. Their cross-model reuse does not import white-noise assumptions into regression.

Confidence benchmarks retain expected length at f alone, with coverage on the pair {f,g}; risk benchmarks retain sup_g inf_estimator max_h ordering. Discrete-design benchmarks are not replaced by white-noise approximations.
Algorithm 1 reaches only Theorem 4.2; Algorithm 2 reaches only Theorem 4.4. Conditional use remains explicit in the surrounding original interval definitions.

The minimum process integral, mixed j indexing and regression block-count exponent are preserved. A magnified crop and PDF glyph baselines distinguish the exponent J-j-1 from a subtraction outside the power.

Every interface has source keywords and meaningful selectors matching its passage, label or related same-paper theorem, plus a source-backed explanation for each related theorem. All mathematical fragments have balanced braces.

source_notes: This audit is specific to the pinned March 2024 preprint. The separate supplementary document containing proofs and technical lemmas was excluded.

Theorem 2.1 retains all four bounds and constants; Theorem 2.2 retains 274 and 3^7; Theorem 3.2 retains (24 times 2^K_alpha minus 3) times 17.5. The exact alpha placement and constant declarations in the remaining Theorems are preserved.
Source bar-X uses the ordinary integral Y_e(t) dt, not dY_e(t). The shift defining the white-noise minimum estimator contains two un-hatted j indices. Neither is corrected.
The regression block count prints denominator 2^(J-j-1), whereas localization uses 2^(J-j). Font-level inspection confirms the complete exponent. The two formulas remain distinct.
Regression selectors use circumflex-accented typewriter letters. The transcription keeps them distinct from white-noise italic selectors and from the caron-accented no-trigger variable.

Unspecified out-of-domain minimum blocks, coarse-level block-count equality, partial regression blocks, small-n algorithm domains, argmin totality and gamma positivity are retained as explicit source notes.

Registered-source revalidation restored LaTeX alpha, rho and varepsilon in naming contexts D6, D7, D9 and D10 after Python escape processing had corrupted them. Original theorem statements, interface statements and dependency relationships are unchanged. Prior artifacts and scripts are archived; source-transcription-corrections.json and evidence/revalidation/artifact-delta.json record the repairs.

unresolved_source_references.detail: Pinned arXiv:2305.00164v2, stamped 10 March 2024. The title and authors match the corpus entry; equality with the journal typeset version is not established.
The source points to a separate supplement for simulation results, comparisons, proofs and technical lemmas. No supplement body was read. This does not omit any main-text Theorem environment.

The source prints bar-X_j,i as the integral of Y_e(t) dt, whereas localization and stopping use dY_l and dY_s. The ordinary process integral is preserved. Replacing it with an increment integral would materially change the estimator and is not performed.
In the two subtracted contrast terms defining tilde-i-hat-j, the first index of tilde-X is an un-hatted j; the other terms use hat-j. The printed mixed indexing is retained.

evidence.location: block sum domain and localization cap

unresolved_source_references.detail: The block-count bound is floor((n+1)/2^(J-j-1)), confirmed by a magnified crop and glyph baselines. The localization cap instead uses floor((n+1)/2^(J-j)). The former allows twice the count of full blocks. No exponent or denominator is silently repaired.

The source explicitly extends localization and stopping increments to infinity outside valid indices, but does not similarly specify bar-X or extend Y_e outside [0,1]. Shifted or expanded minimum-estimation windows can reference such indices. The recorded construction remains partial where the source does not define these values.

The printed equality i_R-i_L=9 times 2^(1+K-tilde_(alpha/4)+K_(alpha/4)) ignores the positive-part truncation in the coarse level when it binds. Both the endpoint definitions and the asserted equality are preserved; no alternate count is substituted.
The regression experiment observes indices 0 through n, but the extra-noise independence sentence refers only to {y_1,...,y_n}. The construction itself includes index 0; the omission is preserved.

evidence.location: I_hi ceiling and intermediate block minimum

unresolved_source_references.detail: The minimum confidence window uses a ceiling that may include a partly out-of-range final block. The source assigns infinity to out-of-range observations while dividing every block by the full block size. No shortened-block average or alternative boundary rule is supplied.

The endpoint algorithms access indices 2 and n-2 and contain ratios of noisy slope expressions. A complete small-n domain, and totalization on all exceptional inputs, is not explicitly stated in the inspected construction. The branch guards and clipping operations are retained as written.
Theorem 2.3 prints gamma<0.1, while log(1/gamma) needs positivity and the following remark explicitly discusses gamma>0. The positivity context is archived separately in A3.

No general deterministic argmin tie rule is supplied. The white-noise stopping definition does not give a fallback for an empty trigger set; the regression construction does explicitly use infinity and cap the level at J. These distinct conventions are preserved.

Regression selectors and the intermediate estimator are printed as circumflex-accented monospaced i, j and f. They are transcribed as hats on math-typewriter letters, not as breve accents or as the white-noise italic selectors. Font inspection and a crop corroborate the distinction.

Algorithm 1 is invoked only when no threshold fires. Algorithm 2 is invoked only when refinement exceeds the finest design level. The local graph records their inclusion in the full interval definitions, while these branch conditions remain in the original statements.
The right line is written v_r,i without the explicit argument (t) on its defining left-hand side, although its formula depends on t and the next line uses v_r,i(t). This source notation is retained.

The inspected class imposes convexity and a unique minimizer. Differentiability, a positive second derivative, and a particular smoothness exponent are not added. The source explicitly states that second derivatives are unnecessary.

ambient_resolution.shared: D1 supplies F, unique Z(f) and M(f). Expectation, absolute loss, confidence coverage, Brownian motion, Gaussian distribution, indicators, finite sums, integrals, argmin, floor/ceiling, positive part and sup/inf use their ordinary mathematical meanings except for the explicit infinity convention A4. A1 supplies Phi,z_alpha and L2 notation; A2 supplies interval length. No library availability is asserted.
ambient_resolution.2.1: White-noise risks D3/D4, expected-length benchmarks D6/D7 and functional moduli D8. Constants a1,A1,b_alpha,B_alpha and alpha range are defined inside the theorem. f in F and epsilon>0 are section-level conventions inherited from D1/D2.
ambient_resolution.2.2: D3/D4/D6/D7 and D1; no edge to the local moduli or water-filling quantities is added merely because those establish the result. All numeric constants are retained.
ambient_resolution.2.3: Arbitrary estimators are quantified inside the theorem, not the later adaptive estimators. D1/D3/D4 resolve the targets and benchmarks. f0,f1,gamma are local binders; positive gamma context is in A3 without rewriting the original theorem.
ambient_resolution.3.1: White-noise estimator D14, horizontal radius D10 and risk D3. The radius depends on the vertical radius D9 by its defining level set. C_z is bound inline.
ambient_resolution.3.2: White-noise interval D15 and coverage D5, horizontal radius D10 and interval benchmark D6. K_alpha is defined inline and also archived as shared calibration D37; C_z,alpha is an alpha-only constant.
ambient_resolution.3.3: White-noise minimum estimator D17 uses the stopping contrasts and printed ordinary-integral quantities D16; vertical radius D9 and minimum risk D4. C_m is bound inline.
ambient_resolution.3.4: White-noise minimum interval D19, coverage D5, vertical radius D9 and minimum length benchmark D7. Its construction uses shared Gaussian-maximum quantile D18 and calibrations D37. The two alpha-dependent constants are inline.
ambient_resolution.4.1: Regression estimator D30 has distinct triggered and no-trigger branches; risk benchmark D22 is defined under n+1 discrete observations D20. C1 is an absolute positive constant, as printed.
ambient_resolution.4.2: Regression interval D32 includes conditional Algorithm 1 (D31). Coverage and expected length use D21/D24. The constructions depend on finite-horizon regression stopping, not white-noise procedures.
ambient_resolution.4.3: Regression minimum estimator D33 includes both branch definitions of its selected block. Its benchmark D23 remains discrete-design, not an epsilon=sigma/sqrt(n) substitution in D4. C3 is not explicitly declared positive in the theorem.
ambient_resolution.4.4: Regression minimum interval D36 uses common setup D34 and conditional Algorithm 2 (D35), plus shared Gaussian calibrations. Coverage and benchmark use D21/D25. The target minimum is explicit in referenced (4.11) although not repeated in the theorem coverage clause.

review_limits: Source fidelity and statement-dependency audit, not proof certification or mathematical repair.
All findings are specific to the pinned preprint; separate supplementary material was excluded.
